title: Surjective quasi-tensor functors of finite tensor categories preserve projectives
difficulty_reason: The author introduces the Frobenius–Perron weight p(X) of nonprojective Krull–Schmidt summands and proves the tensor submultiplicativity using the projective tensor ideal. Multiplication of the indecomposable projectives gives the strictly positive matrix B. The inequalities (sum_i p_i)p≥Bp and p_i≤FPdim(P_i), together with the spectral radius of B, force either zero defect or complete saturation. The author then uses surjectivity in the corrected any-object subquotient sense, exactness, and projectivity plus injectivity to split a nonzero target projective out of the image of a source projective, contradicting saturation. This spectral/defect argument remains new after charging the earlier projective-ideal, duality and FPdim results.
